description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup known for its comforting warmth and rich flavor. This vibrant, creamy soup is a staple in Turkish cuisine, often enjoyed as a starter or a light meal. It is incredibly easy to prepare, offering a delicious taste of Turkey in every spoonful.

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables and Lentils
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. Drain them well. Finely chop the onion, dice the carrot, and dice the potato, ensuring pieces are similar in size for even cooking.

instructions.title: Saute Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the diced carrot and potato, and cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

instructions.title: Combine and Simmer
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, letting it toast slightly. Add the rinsed red lentils, water or broth, salt, and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup until it is completely smooth and creamy. If you dont have an immersion blender, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot. Be careful when blending hot liquids.

instructions.title: Prepare the Mint Butter Sauce
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Once the butter is melted and slightly foamy, add the dried mint and red pepper flakes (pul biber). Cook for about 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Be careful not to burn the spices.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Pour the hot mint butter sauce directly into the blended soup, stirring gently to incorporate some of it. Ladle the Mercimek Corbasi into individual bowls. Drizzle a little extra mint butter sauce on top of each serving and garnish with fresh lemon wedges. Serve hot.

tips: For extra depth of flavor, roast the vegetables slightly before adding them to the pot.
Adjust the consistency of the soup by adding more hot water or broth if you prefer a thinner soup after blending.
Always serve Mercimek Corbasi with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice; it brightens the flavors beautifully.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of Turkish cuisine, where warmth, comfort, and incredible flavor come together in a bowl of Mercimek Corbasi. This vibrant red lentil soup is more than just a dish; it's a staple, a hug in a bowl, and a testament to the simplicity and richness of Turkish cooking. Loved by all ages, from bustling city cafes to cozy family kitchens, Mercimek Corbasi offers a delightful blend of earthy lentils, aromatic spices, and a silky-smooth texture that makes it utterly irresistible. Whether you're seeking a nutritious meal, a comforting starter, or an authentic taste of Turkey, this iconic soup promises to deliver. Get ready to discover the magic behind one of the world's most cherished lentil soups, and learn how to bring its heartwarming essence right into your home.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi (Turkish Red Lentil Soup)?

Mercimek Corbasi, pronounced mer-jee-MEK chor-ba-SUH, is a quintessential Turkish soup renowned for its beautiful reddish-orange hue and incredibly smooth, creamy texture. At its core, it's a humble dish made primarily from red lentils, yet it explodes with complex flavors thanks to a careful selection of aromatic ingredients. Unlike many lentil soups that might be chunky, the signature of Mercimek Corbasi lies in its velvety consistency, achieved by blending the cooked lentils until perfectly smooth.

This soup holds a special place in Turkish culture. It's often the first course at almost any meal, from breakfast to dinner, and is particularly cherished during colder months or when one needs a boost of comforting nourishment. It's known for being both incredibly healthy and deeply satisfying, packed with protein, fiber, and essential nutrients. The flavor profile is savory and earthy, often brightened with a touch of tangy tomato paste and finished with a fragrant drizzle of butter infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes – a crucial element that adds both visual appeal and a burst of aromatic spice. It’s a soup that embodies the soul of Turkish hospitality: simple, wholesome, and profoundly delicious.

## Ingredients You'll Need for Mercimek Corbasi

Creating an authentic Mercimek Corbasi requires a few key ingredients, most of which are pantry staples. Here’s what you’ll need to gather for a batch that serves 4-6 people:

*   **1 cup (about 200g) Red Lentils:** Washed thoroughly until the water runs clear. These break down easily, giving the soup its signature smoothness.
*   **1 medium Yellow Onion:** Finely chopped, forms the aromatic base.
*   **2-3 cloves Garlic:** Minced, for depth of flavor.
*   **2 tablespoons Olive Oil or Butter:** For sautéing.
*   **1 tablespoon Tomato Paste (Salça):** Adds a rich umami depth and a subtle tang, contributing to the soup's color.
*   **6-7 cups (1.4-1.6 liters) Vegetable or Chicken Broth (or water):** The liquid base. Broth adds more flavor, but water works perfectly fine.
*   **1 teaspoon Dried Mint (Kuru Nane):** Essential for that distinct Turkish aroma.
*   **½ - 1 teaspoon Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber or Maras Biber):** For a gentle warmth and color. Adjust to your spice preference.
*   **Salt and Black Pepper:** To taste.
*   **Fresh Lemon Wedges:** For serving, absolutely essential for brightening the flavors.
*   **Optional for Garnish (Nane Yağı):**
    *   **2 tablespoons Butter:** Melted.
    *   **1 teaspoon Dried Mint:** Added to the melted butter.
    *   **½ teaspoon Red Pepper Flakes:** Added to the melted butter.

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Mercimek Corbasi

Making Mercimek Corbasi is straightforward, even for novice cooks. Follow these steps for a perfect bowl:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water in a fine-mesh sieve until the water runs completely clear. This removes any starch and ensures a cleaner flavor. Set aside to drain.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent, being careful not to brown them. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
3.  **Build the Base:** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. This step helps to deepen its flavor and mellow its acidity.
4.  **Add Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed lentils to the pot, stirring to combine them with the onion and tomato paste mixture. Pour in the vegetable or chicken broth (or water). Bring the mixture to a boil.
5.  **Simmer and Cook:** Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
6.  **Blend to Smoothness:** Remove the pot from the heat. Carefully use an immersion blender to blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. Alternatively, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot.
7.  **Season and Finish:** Return the pot to low heat. Stir in the dried mint, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot broth or water until it reaches your desired consistency.
8.  **Prepare the Garnish (Optional but Recommended):** In a small saucepan, melt the butter over low heat. Add the dried mint and red pepper flakes and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the mint. Remove from heat.

## Pro Tips for the Best Mercimek Corbasi

While Mercimek Corbasi is simple, a few professional tips can elevate your soup from good to truly exceptional:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This is crucial. Unrinsed lentils can make your soup cloudy and sometimes impart an earthy, slightly bitter taste. Keep rinsing until the water is clear.
*   **Don't Skip the Tomato Paste Sauté:** Cooking the tomato paste for a minute or two before adding the liquid caramelizes it slightly, developing a deeper, richer flavor and color for your Mercimek Corbasi.
*   **Blend Until Velvety Smooth:** The hallmark of authentic Mercimek Corbasi is its silky texture. An immersion blender makes this easy, but a regular blender works perfectly. Ensure there are no grainy bits left.
*   **The Power of the Nane Yağı (Mint Butter Drizzle):** While optional, the simple butter infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes (nane yağı) is a game-changer. It adds a beautiful aroma, a touch of richness, and that signature vibrant finish. Don't overheat it; just let the flavors infuse gently.
*   **Fresh Lemon is Non-Negotiable:** A generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice at the table is absolutely essential. It brightens all the flavors, adds a crucial tangy counterpoint, and elevates the entire experience. Encourage everyone to add it to their bowl.
*   **Adjust Consistency:** If your soup is too thick after blending, simply whisk in a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your preferred consistency. If it's too thin, simmer it gently for a few more minutes to reduce.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Turkish Lentil Soup

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways. Here are some traditional and delicious serving suggestions:

*   **With a Squeeze of Lemon:** As mentioned, a fresh lemon wedge on the side for each serving is paramount. The bright acidity cuts through the richness and lifts the earthy notes of the lentils.
*   **A Drizzle of Nane Yağı:** Spoon the fragrant mint and chili-infused butter directly into the center of each bowl just before serving for an aromatic and visually appealing finish.
*   **Crusty Bread:** Serve alongside a basket of fresh, crusty bread like Turkish pide, simit (sesame bread rings), or even a simple baguette for dipping and soaking up every last drop.
*   **Pickles (Turşu):** In Turkey, it's common to serve soups with a side of mixed pickles, which provide a delightful tangy crunch that contrasts beautifully with the smooth soup.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprinkle of fresh parsley or dill can add a touch of freshness and color.
*   **As a Starter or Light Meal:** Mercimek Corbasi makes an excellent appetizer for a larger Turkish meal, but it's also hearty enough to be a light and satisfying main course, especially when paired with bread and a simple salad.
*   **Yogurt (Optional):** While less common for red lentil soup, some people enjoy a dollop of plain yogurt, particularly with spicier versions, to add a creamy, cooling element.

## Variations and Dietary Adaptations

One of the beauties of Mercimek Corbasi is its inherent adaptability, making it suitable for various dietary needs and taste preferences:

*   **Vegan/Vegetarian:** This soup is naturally vegan if you use vegetable broth or water, and olive oil instead of butter for sautéing the aromatics. For the optional garnish, use olive oil instead of butter.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Red lentils are naturally gluten-free, and as long as you use gluten-free broth, this soup is entirely safe for those avoiding gluten.
*   **Spicier Version:** If you love heat, feel free to increase the amount of red pepper flakes (pul biber) in both the soup itself and the butter garnish. You could even add a pinch of cayenne pepper for an extra kick.
*   **Adding Vegetables:** While the classic recipe focuses on lentils and aromatics, you can certainly add finely diced carrots, potatoes, or celery along with the onions for extra nutrients and a slightly different texture. Add them at the beginning with the onions and cook until tender before blending.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** A pinch of smoked paprika added with the tomato paste can introduce a lovely, subtle smoky depth to the soup.
*   **Creamier Texture (Less Traditional):** For an even richer, creamier soup, some non-traditional variations might include a splash of milk or cream after blending, though this isn't typical in authentic Turkish preparation.
*   **Herbal Variations:** While dried mint is standard, a tiny amount of dried oregano or thyme can also be added during the simmering phase for a different aromatic twist, though mint remains the star.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a soup; it's a culinary embrace, a dish that nourishes both body and soul. Its rich history, simple ingredients, and comforting warmth make it a beloved staple across Turkey and increasingly, around the world. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a beginner in the kitchen, mastering this Turkish red lentil soup is a rewarding experience that will bring a taste of authentic Mediterranean hospitality to your table. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to fall in love with the timeless appeal of Mercimek Corbasi.
